root_cause.text: The Octeontx2 AF driver dereferenced `rvu->fwdata` without first verifying that firmware-shared MAC/channel data had been mapped, so on systems booted without a MAC block the `rvu_sdp_init()` and CGX link-mode paths could access a NULL/uninitialized `fwdata` pointer and crash.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit `if (!rvu->fwdata)` / `if (rvu->fwdata && rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid)` checks in `rvu_cgx.c` and `rvu_sdp.c`, and the commit message states that “Accessing fwdata, on boards booted with out MAC block leading to kernel panics,” with the crash occurring in `rvu_sdp_init+0x18/0x114`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds explicit `if (!rvu->fwdata)` / `if (rvu->fwdata && rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid)` checks in `rvu_cgx.c` and `rvu_sdp.c`, and the commit message states that “Accessing fwdata, on boards booted with out MAC block leading to kernel panics,” with the crash occurring in `rvu_sdp_init+0x18/0x114`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to reject CGX link mode requests when firmware data is not mapped.
intent_record.what: A new early return was added at the start of rvu_mbox_handler_cgx_set_link_mode(): if rvu->fwdata is NULL, the function now returns LMAC_AF_ERR_FIRMWARE_DATA_NOT_MAPPED before performing the existing permission check and further processing.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the handler now refuses to proceed when firmware data has not been mapped, preventing later code from operating on unavailable fwdata and returning a specific firmware-mapping error instead of continuing normally.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null-pointer guard before accessing fwdata in rvu_sdp_init() to prevent a crash during SDP initialization.
intent_record.what: The condition in rvu_sdp_init() was changed from checking only rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid to first verifying rvu->fwdata is non-NULL and then checking channel_data.valid.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents dereferencing rvu->fwdata when it is NULL, avoiding a potential null-pointer access during SDP initialization while preserving the existing behavior when fwdata is present and valid.

Add a null-pointer guard before accessing fwdata in rvu_sdp_init() to prevent a crash during SDP initialization.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adding a check before using firmware-shared data, preventing CGX link mode paths from dereferencing an unmapped or NULL `fwdata` pointer.
The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a null-pointer check before dereferencing rvu->fwdata in rvu_sdp_init(), preventing the crash caused by missing firmware-shared MAC/channel data.

candidates.rationale: This statement dereferences rvu->fwdata without first checking whether fwdata is mapped or non-NULL. If fwdata is uninitialized on systems without a MAC block, this access can crash during SDP initialization.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line dereferences rvu->fwdata without first verifying that the firmware-shared data pointer is mapped or non-NULL. On systems without a MAC block, fwdata may be uninitialized, causing a NULL/uninitialized pointer access during SDP initialization.

    Octeontx2-af: Fetch MAC channel info from firmware
    
    Packet ingress and egress MAC/serdes channel numbers are configurable
    on CN10K series of silicons. These channel numbers inturn used while
    installing MCAM rules to match ingress/egress port. Fetch these channel
    numbers from firmware at driver init time.
    
    Signed-off-by: Hariprasad K
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly dereferences firmware-shared data without a null check: `if (rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid) { ... pfvf->sdp_info = &rvu->fwdata->channel_data.info; }`. This matches the root cause because `rvu->fwdata` is accessed before verifying that firmware data has been mapped, so on systems without the MAC/firmware block it can still crash. The code shown does not add any guard like `if (!rvu->fwdata) return ...;`, so the fix for safe access is not present here.
